messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Meridian Corp (enterprise tenant) reporting elevated 502/504 errors from east1-dedicated pool. Error rate +42% over baseline, latency spikes. Auto-escalation threshold hit. paging oncall: Samir. :rotating_light:
Samir (oncall-sre): Ack — I’m on it. Starting triage. Any immediate customer-facing impact known?
Julia (acct-mgr): Hey Samir — Meridian reported user-facing timeouts in their admin console, some jobs failing. They flagged billing-sensitive workflows. They want status updates. I’m on standby to coordinate comms.
Samir (oncall-sre): Thanks. I’m checking pool health, qps by tenant, and recent deploys. @deploy-bot can you show last deploys to east1-dedicated in past 2 hours?
deploy-bot: recent deploys to east1-dedicated:
- 2367887000: runtime v3.12.4 (canary)
- 2367889000: autoscaler tweak (rolling)
- 2367890000: model-weights refresh (small)
Samir (oncall-sre): Good. I’m pulling logs now.
Samir (oncall-sre): Logs show repeated "KV cache miss + OOM retry" traces from worker nodes serving Meridian shard m-42. Sample:
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] worker-17 east1 m-42 ERROR: allocate failed: cuda OOM trying to reserve 512MB
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] worker-17 east1 m-42 RETRY: request queued, latency 1800ms
```
Kai (netops): If it’s OOM on dedicated pool, warm capacity might be insufficient. Are we seeing memory pressure across the pool or just that shard?
Devin (runtime): Looks localized to m-42. Memory logging shows KV cache growth after long-running sessions from Meridian jobs. Could be leaky session pattern. Rolling restart of affected nodes should free KV cache.
Samir (oncall-sre): Plan: 1) Spin up warm nodes in east1-dedicated (burst) for Meridian shard. 2) Shift a portion of Meridian traffic to eu-west-3 dedicated pool (where they have warm capacity). 3) Lower DNS TTL for their CNAME and coordinate with their DNS team for a controlled cutover if necessary. 4) Continue node restarts and patch mem limits.
Samir (oncall-sre): @Kai can you provision +5 warm GPUs to east1-dedicated for Meridian (tag m-42) and confirm scheduler placement? Use burst capacity, do not affect other tenants.
Kai (netops): On it. Provisioning request submitted:
```
POST /api/v1/pools/east1-dedicated/burst
{ "tenant_tag": "m-42", "gpus": 5, "priority": "burst" }
```
Kai (netops): ETA ~90s for nodes to register. Scheduler will pin by tenant_tag.
Samir (oncall-sre): Good. @Devin start rolling restart of worker-17 and worker-19 only. Mark them draining first. Keep m-42 shard pinned to avoid split-brain.
Devin (runtime): Starting drain -> restart on worker-17,19. Commands:
```
runtimectl drain worker-17 --shard m-42 --grace 30s
restart worker-17 --now
```
Devin (runtime): Restart done for worker-17. KV cache cleared. Observing reduced OOM traces on that node.
Samir (oncall-sre): Nice. Kai — any update on burst nodes?
Kai (netops): +5 GPUs registered and healthy. New nodes labeled [east1-burst-01..05]. Network routes configured.
Samir (oncall-sre): Ok — now prepare traffic shift plan. We’ll do canary redirect ~10% of Meridian traffic to eu-west-3 dedicated. If healthy, increase to 50% then 100% if needed. @Accounts-bot, reduce Meridian CNAME TTL to 60s for safe cutover. Also notify their DNS team via email thread.
Accounts-bot: TTL change request queued. Reminder: TTL change propagates per authoritative config; external registrars may take longer.
Samir (oncall-sre): Implementing canary via traffic manager: route 10% by weight to eu-west-3-meridian pool. Command:
```
rb-trafficctl set-weight --tenant m-42 --from east1 --to eu-west-3 --weight 10
```
Samir (oncall-sre): Executed. Monitoring latency/errors on both pools.
Maya (oncall-sre): I’m watching metrics dashboard. Canary looks good so far — error rate on eu-west-3 is normal, latency ~150ms, no OOMs. East1 error rate dropped 30% after restarts + burst nodes.
Samir (oncall-sre): Increase to 50% now.
Samir (oncall-sre): Executed weight=50. Keep canary for 3 min and check.
Devin (runtime): Observing request distribution, backend saturation decreased. KV working set on east1 is stabilizing. Still seeing occasional 502 spikes on a small subset — probably long sessions migrating.
Julia (acct-mgr): Meridian’s SRE on their side reports some queued jobs now running on eu-west-3. They asked for an ETA on full cutover.
Samir (oncall-sre): If we get steady state at 50% for 5min with no regressions, we’ll move to 100% and then scale down east1-dedicated shard for Meridian. Need explicit approval from Accounts for customer-visible DNS changes. @Julia can you confirm if Meridian is okay with immediate full shift if metrics hold?
Julia (acct-mgr): Confirmed — Meridian approves full shift once their QA gives a quick thumbs in next 4–5 mins. I’ll wait on their signal.
Samir (oncall-sre): Thanks. Monitoring for 5m.
Samir (oncall-sre): 5m check complete: eu-west-3 healthy, east1 stabilized. Proceeding to 100% shift.
Samir (oncall-sre): Executing weight=100.
Samir (oncall-sre): Executed. Traffic now routed to eu-west-3 for Meridian. Observability: errors fell to baseline, latency steady.
Kai (netops): Adjusting peering for full shift completed. No routing errors.
Samir (oncall-sre): Next: scale down east1 m-42 shard instances to one warm node for safety, and leave the burst nodes to drain. Also file an action item to investigate KV cache growth pattern with runtime team.
Devin (runtime): Filing ticket: RUNTIME-4386 "Investigate KV cache lifecycle for Meridian jobs (m-42)". Will look for mem leak or unbounded session retention.
Maya (oncall-sre): I need to take over monitoring for the 02:00 UTC window. Samir, handoff in 15m?
Samir (oncall-sre): Yup — handing to Maya in 15. Key context: root cause likely KV cache growth on long-running sessions for Meridian; mitigation: traffic shifted to eu-west-3, restarted problematic nodes, burst added. Customer impacted briefly (timeouts), but core flows recovered.
Maya (oncall-sre): Got it. I’ll keep watch and escalate if error rate >5% above baseline.
Julia (acct-mgr): I sent Meridian a short update: "We detected elevated errors, shifted your traffic to alternate region, full recovery observed. Our engineers will follow up with root cause and remediation plan." They acknowledged and thanked the team.
Samir (oncall-sre): Closing incident channel for live ops. Will open postmortem doc and tag oncall and runtime leads. Action items:
- RUNTIME-4386 investigate KV cache
- OPS-3342 improve burst gating to avoid cross-tenant impact
- COMM-2201 follow-up update to Meridian with timeline
Samir (oncall-sre): Thanks everyone. Maya takeover note: I’ll DM the handoff checklist and logs. :white_check_mark:
Maya (oncall-sre): Received, thanks. I’m marking this monitored and will update if anything regresses.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Status changed -> mitigated. Severity: SEV3 -> monitoring. Incident channel will remain open for 1h for observation.
